title: A galaxy on the edge
caption: The edge-on spiral galaxy NGC 5023, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 5023 · constellation Canes Venatici · about 33 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: We see the spiral galaxy NGC 5023 edge-on in this Hubble image. Its arms are hidden by the angle, but the slim profile of its disc stretches across the frame. It lies over 30 million light-years away.

NGC 5023 belongs to the M51 group, whose brightest member is the Whirlpool Galaxy. By comparison NGC 5023 keeps to itself, sitting fairly isolated from its neighbors. It is still popular with astronomers, because edge-on discs let them study what lies above and below a galaxy's central plane.

By sorting the stars there by type and by how far along they are in their lives, researchers learn how galaxies evolve. A study of six edge-on spirals, including this one, found a trend suggesting that heating of the disc helps explain the stars found away from the plane. Hubble's sharp view picks out over 30 000 separate bright stars.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.33 x 2.86 arcminutes) and distance (33 million light years), the frame spans roughly 32,000 × 27,000 light-years. Its light set out about 33 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using a visible and a near-infrared filter. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: No eye could separate individual stars in a galaxy this far away, and part of the data is near-infrared light we cannot see.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Those 30 000 stars are only a small fraction of the several billion the galaxy holds, and the rest are too faint to separate even with Hubble.
NGC 5023 is also one of 14 disc galaxies in the GHOSTS survey, the largest study so far of the stars living in the outer regions of disc galaxies.
alt: A thin, edge-on spiral galaxy stretched across the frame, its disc seen in profile.
